claims.text: Trace oxygen introduced during synthesis forms ordered oxygen complexes at nanoparticle interfaces.
Ordered oxygen complexes pin grain boundaries.
Grain-boundary pinning by ordered oxygen complexes stabilizes the solid-solution structure under high-temperature catalytic and thermoelectric conditions.
Non-equiatomic MnFeCoNiCu can form a stable single-phase alloy.
The proposed initial material consists of MnFeCoNiCu nanoparticles synthesized without oxygen doping.
Undoped MnFeCoNiCu nanoparticles have greater grain-boundary mobility than oxygen-doped particles.
Undoped MnFeCoNiCu nanoparticles tend to segregate and coarsen under harsh service conditions.
Approximately 3 at.% oxygen will be introduced during synthesis by controlling the oxygen partial pressure.
Approximately 3 at.% oxygen promotes formation of ordered oxygen complexes at nanoparticle interfaces.
The particles will be cycled through 773–1173 K catalytic conditions and 473–1923 K thermoelectric conditions under alternating reductive and oxidative environments.
Ordered oxygen complexes form at grain boundaries and other interfacial regions in the nanoparticles.
Ordered oxygen complexes pin local atomic clusters and limit atomic mobility.
Limiting species mobility favors retention or formation of a single HEA phase by suppressing secondary-phase development.
Limiting atomic mobility through oxygen-complex pinning suppresses high-temperature coarsening.
Oxygen-doped nanoparticles will retain a more homogeneous single-phase structure than undoped controls.
Oxygen-doped nanoparticles will exhibit less grain growth and elemental segregation than undoped controls.
Improved structural stability will produce superior catalytic and thermoelectric performance.
Above a critical oxygen concentration, bulk oxide formation becomes favored over interfacial ordered oxygen-complex formation.
Bulk oxide formation compromises the proposed stabilization effect.
Support-related interactions may dominate over oxygen-complex stabilization in some systems.

contradictions.description: The baseline is described as being synthesized without trace oxygen, whereas the experimental control is defined only as having no intentional oxygen doping. The latter can still contain adventitious oxygen, so the control state is not consistently specified.

The hypothesis describes oxygen partial pressure as approximately 3 at.%, but atomic percent is a composition unit rather than a partial-pressure unit. The intended synthesis control variable is therefore ambiguous.
